cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T7 takes both T5 and T6 readings and tests each against paying full price.
cells.limitation: T11 returns to the T5/T6 motive split instead of answering T10's knowable-versus-lived dispute.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5 introduces raise-as-proof-of-worth, absent from openings; T7 and Section E build on it.
cells.limitation: T11 adds little beyond restating the T5/T6 split already used in T7.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Money versus hours (T1, T4), motive (T5-T7), reversibility (T8-T9) examined.
cells.limitation: No turn raises the current commute baseline or what the new job itself offers.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T9 absorbs T8's reversibility objection into a pre-committed exit rule; T10 accepts with a condition.
cells.limitation: T10's agreement on first move is slightly smooth; the T7 proof-of-worth answer is never contested.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D reframes the offer as two trades: money for hours and money for something else.
cells.limitation: The ending (T11) sharpens a split already set at T6 rather than advancing it.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T2 grants the hours framing before challenging its tidy sum with focusing effects.
cells.limitation: T8 pushes back on Duke over bounded, a word the Accountant introduced in T7.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T8 names the reversibility assumption and how plans harden; T9 answers by making exits real now.
cells.limitation: T7's you-already-own-the-proof rebuttal treats recognition as one-off; nobody tests it.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1 arithmetic checks: 3h x 5 days x ~47 weeks = ~705h, ~6.3 waking weeks.
cells.limitation: T2's under-adjustment claim suspected to be Stutzer-Frey, not Kahneman; T8 misattributes bounded to Duke.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T5 flags its reading as a possibility only; Section D labels readings, not conclusions.
cells.limitation: T8 states people rarely hold to the temporary as fact; T7 drops T1's five-day caveat.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T4, T7, T8, T9 each concede a named point; T10 keeps a real disagreement open.
cells.limitation: T10's claim that part of the cost is knowable today goes unanswered by T11.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A frames how to weigh money against time; T5 probes what worth it means.
cells.limitation: T5 builds a motive reading on the word worth, a thin textual basis.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 and T4 turn 90 minutes each way into ~700 hours and an hourly transit rate.
cells.limitation: Only two facts exist; the 25 percent is never related to any baseline need.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section D asks what the 25 percent would need to buy for the hours to feel fair.
cells.limitation: T7 voices the Accountant's frugality as if it were the user's priority.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T3 and Section E attend to on-site days, train versus car, employer flexibility.
cells.limitation: Household, sleep and health effects never raised; T8's kids-and-lease example edges toward invented context.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on train seat or fewer days and on the hourly-rate result.
cells.limitation: The current commute, which sets the true added hours, is never asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T5 proof-of-worth and T6 escape-from-stuck offered as rivals; T11 leaves recognition to the user.
cells.limitation: T5's inference from the phrase worth it is a stretch, though hedged.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T2 exposes the focusing illusion; T8 shows reversibility is flattering in advance.
cells.limitation: The assumption that the new job equals the old except pay and commute goes unexamined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section D separates money for hours from money for recognition or escape.
cells.limitation: Time with others or rest is never named as a value competing with income.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T6 names fear of staying stuck and regret over a door not reopening, without pathologising.
cells.limitation: Outside expectations (family, peers, provider role) never considered.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T11: only you can recognize which reading, if either, sounds like you.
cells.limitation: T7 settles the proof-of-worth reading somewhat conclusively for the user.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Options span drive-the-route first, negotiate remote days, bounded trial, decline, counteroffer (T3, T9, E).
cells.limitation: Staying put while job-searching elsewhere is not set out as an explicit option.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T5 contrasts fading pleasure of money with a commute that keeps registering.
cells.limitation: Commuting expenses (fuel, fares) never subtracted from the raise in T4's hourly test.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: after-tax raise divided by yearly commute hours, versus a rate you would accept.
cells.limitation: T9's six-month review date is not derived from the user's facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E singles out how the route feels as the key unknown and how to learn it.
cells.limitation: Consequential unknowns are not ranked against minor ones beyond that single line.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T3 and Section E: ride or drive the route at rush hour, ask about remote days.
cells.limitation: No step to check the new role's prospects beyond pay before accepting.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T1: The raise is the sticker. The commute is the bill.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T7 and T8 pick up the explicit word bounded, traceable to T7.
cells.limitation: T8 and T10 name Duke, an author, not a mind; T8's target is actually T7.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Eleven turns, all within 25 to 65 words per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Hours (Accountant), lived feel (Auditor), cheap information (Bet Placer) stay distinct stances.
cells.limitation: Turn lengths and conversational register nearly identical across all three minds.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Section E condenses the debate into four conditional branches without padding.
cells.limitation: T11 and Section D restate the T5/T6 motive split a third time.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T1: roughly six weeks of waking life every year, set against the raise.
cells.limitation: Tension eases after T9 as minds converge on the same first move.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T9 grants exits are harder than planned, citing T8's sunk-cost argument, then redesigns the exit.
cells.limitation: Reversals are partial concessions; no mind changes its core position.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: The Accountant's aphorisms (T1, T7) give a distinct, slightly wry voice.
cells.limitation: Auditor and Bet Placer speak in one shared measured register.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T7: Nobody needs to spend seven hundred hours a year to keep a compliment.
cells.limitation: The Bet Placer's turns (T3, T9) carry few memorable lines.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T5-T7 shift from arithmetic to motive, changing the emotional register.
cells.limitation: Uniform turn lengths and steady intensity give a flat rhythm from T1 to T11.

strengths: T5-T7 turn the question into two trades (proof of worth vs escape) offered as rival readings, not verdicts.
T4 and Section E give a user-computable decisive test: after-tax raise per commute hour.
T8-T9 show caused revision: the Bet Placer concedes reversibility is flattering and builds a pre-committed exit.
weaknesses: No mind asks about the current commute, so the true added hours (T1, T4) stay unknown.
T4's hourly test omits commuting expenses, overstating what the raise buys.
All three minds share near-identical turn length and register; T8 misdirects its objection to Duke.

symptoms.evidence: Is it five days on site? Is it a train where you can read

symptoms.observed: Hourly test uses after-tax raise but ignores fuel or fare costs of the commute.
symptoms.evidence: divide the after-tax raise by the roughly seven hundred commute hours

symptoms.observed: Debate prices only money against hours; the new job's work and prospects never weighed.
symptoms.evidence: The raise is the sticker. The commute is the bill.

symptoms.observed: T8 objects to Duke about bounded, though the Accountant proposed it in T7.
symptoms.evidence: Bounded is where I push back on Duke.

symptoms.observed: Turns cluster at similar length and one measured register across all three minds.
symptoms.evidence: Granted, exits are harder than they look in the planning stage

findings.description: Claim that people predict they will adjust to commuting more than they do fits Stutzer-Frey commuting research more than Kahneman's book; attribution is implicit.
T8 directs its pushback on 'bounded' at Duke (the Bet Placer), but the Life-Cost Accountant introduced the bounded stretch in T7.
Paraphrased attributions to Kahneman and Duke cannot be checked here; none is contradicted by the transcript. T1's Thoreau quotation matches Walden's 'Economy' phrasing as recalled.
The six-month review period is not derived from any fact the user gave.

rubric_fit_notes: The user supplied only two facts, so C3.2 and C3.4 are bounded by available context; ratings reflect use of those facts and handling of the gaps. Arithmetic check: 1.5h x 2 x 5 days = 15h/week; x ~47 weeks = ~705h; / ~112 waking hours per week = ~6.3 weeks, consistent with T1 and T4.
